title: Signature Lineage-Bred Prompts
description: Signature edition: every evolved prompt carries its full evolutionary lineage — parent prompts, mutations applied, fitness history across generations. Anyone can trace a champion prompt back through its ancestry and see exactly which mutation earned each gain. Prompts become bred artifacts with pedigrees. This is a Signature original method.
method: Each generation records (prompt, parents, mutation, fitness); the champion's pedigree is queryable; promising dead branches can be revived.
usage: Archive every generation, not just champions; mine pedigrees for reusable mutation patterns.

title: Signature OPRO optimization by LLM
description: Signature edition: OPRO (Optimization by PROmpting) uses an LLM as the optimizer: it reads the history of past prompts and their scores, then proposes new prompts likely to score higher — meta-prompting where the model does the prompt engineering. Google showed LLMs can iteratively improve prompts and even discover better optimization trajectories than hand-designed ones.
method: Meta-prompt contains (prompt, score) history; the optimizer LLM proposes candidates; candidates are scored on the dev set; history grows; repeat.
usage: Give the optimizer a clear objective and diverse history; score candidates on enough examples to be stable.

demo.code:
history = [('Answer briefly.', 0.62), ('Think step by step, then answer.', 0.81)]
print('optimizer sees history:', history)
print('optimizer proposes: "Decompose the problem, solve each part, then summarize."')

title: Signature Instruction induction from examples
description: Signature edition: Instead of hand-writing instructions, instruction induction shows the model input/output pairs and asks it to write the instruction that explains the pattern (Honovich et al.). The induced instruction often outperforms human guesses because it's written in the model's own 'dialect'.
method: Provide few-shot pairs; ask the model to induce the instruction; score candidate instructions on held-out pairs; keep the best.
usage: Use diverse pairs covering edge cases; verify the induced instruction on held-out data.

demo.code:
pairs = [('2,3', '5'), ('10,4', '14')]
print('pairs:', pairs)
print('induced instruction: "Add the two numbers." (score 1.0 on held-out)')

title: Signature Fitness with multi-objective scores
description: Signature edition: Real prompts trade off accuracy, cost, latency, and safety. Multi-objective evolution (NSGA-II style) keeps a Pareto front of prompts — no single winner, but the best accuracy-for-cost options — so operators can pick the right tradeoff per use case instead of pretending one prompt fits all.
method: Score each prompt on all objectives; keep non-dominated solutions (Pareto front); select parents from the front; evolve toward a better frontier.
usage: Normalize objectives before comparing; present the frontier with tradeoff labels for human selection.

demo.code:
front = [('pA', 0.9, 0.05), ('pB', 0.85, 0.01)]  # (acc, cost)
print('Pareto front (acc, cost):', front)
print('operator picks pB for cheap tier, pA for quality tier')

title: Signature Adversarial prompt robustness search
description: Signature edition: Evolve prompts against adversarial inputs: the fitness function includes worst-case performance over attack suites (jailbreaks, confusing phrasing, edge cases). Prompts that survive evolution are robust by selection, not by hope.
method: Fitness = weighted mean of clean accuracy and adversarial-suite score; evolve; track robustness separately from accuracy.
usage: Keep the adversarial suite fresh; a prompt robust against last year's attacks may fail this year's.

title: Signature Prompt distillation to smaller models
description: Signature edition: A big model's evolved prompt often doesn't transfer to a small model. Prompt distillation re-runs the optimization loop with the small model as the scorer, finding the phrasing that works best for that specific model — prompts are model-specific, and evolution finds each model's dialect.
method: Take the champion prompt; run evolution with the small model scoring; keep the small-model champion; verify the quality/cost tradeoff.
usage: Never assume transfer; always re-optimize for the deployment model; measure the final tradeoff.

demo.code:
print('big-model champion: "Decompose, solve, summarize." (0.91)')
print('re-optimized for 1B model: "Steps: 1) parts 2) answers 3) final" (0.84)')
print('deployed: 10x cheaper at 0.84 vs 0.91')

title: Signature Prompt mutation operators
description: Signature edition: Effective evolution needs good mutations: paraphrase the instruction, add/remove constraints, swap example order, change tone, add a format specification. A library of mutation operators applied systematically explores the prompt space far better than random word tweaks.
method: Define operators (paraphrase, add-constraint, drop-constraint, reorder-examples, tone-shift, add-format); apply randomly per generation; track which operators produce winners.
usage: Log which mutations win; retire operators that never help; combine winning operators.

demo.code:
ops = ['paraphrase', 'add-constraint', 'tone-shift']
print('mutation:', ops[1], '-> "Answer in under 50 words." gains constraint')
print('operator win rates tracked across generations')

title: Signature DSPy compiled prompts
description: Signature edition: DSPy treats prompts as programs to compile: you declare the pipeline structure and metrics, and DSPy's teleprompters (COPRO, MIPRO) search over instructions and few-shot examples to maximize the metric. The output is an optimized, versioned prompt program — prompt engineering as compilation.
method: Define module signatures and metric; choose a teleprompter; it proposes instruction/example combos, evaluates on the dev set, and returns the compiled program.
usage: Invest in the metric and dev set — the compiler optimizes exactly what you measure.

demo.code:
print('dspy.Module: question -> answer')
print('teleprompter MIPRO searches instructions x few-shot examples')
print('compiled: best combo on dev metric, versioned artifact')

title: Signature Bandit-based prompt selection
description: Signature edition: When several prompt candidates compete in production, multi-armed bandits (UCB, Thompson sampling) allocate traffic to learn which is best while exploiting the current leader. The system continuously tests and converges — prompt selection as an online learning problem.
method: Each prompt is an arm; pull = serve with that prompt; reward = task success; UCB/Thompson sampling balances exploration and exploitation.
usage: Define the reward cleanly; start with uniform exploration; let the bandit shift traffic as evidence accumulates.
